correctness.rationale: For SPD K and positive diagonal A the symmetric derivative is similar to I+h S^{1/2}D(z)S^{1/2}, S=A^{1/2}KA^{1/2}. For distinct lift points v=x−y, strict global sine secant >−v_i² gives v^T K^{−1}(F~(x)−F~(y))>v^T K^{−1}v−h v^TAv≥(λ^{-1}−h)v^TAv, strictly positive for h≤1/λ. Properness and Z^n equivariance yield a torus homeomorphism at the singular endpoint. For h<1/λ the Jacobian is positive/invertible; at z_i=π the critical Jacobian has zero eigenvalue. At any h>1/λ choose t=1/(hλ)−δ and a one-coordinate cosine perturbation −ε, with δ/u_j²<ε<1−t for an eigenvector coordinate u_j≠0: I−htS is positive definite and the perturbation rank-one negative, so the Jacobian has precisely one negative eigenvalue and is regular orientation-reversing. Degree one then forces at least three regular preimages on a nonempty open set of regular targets. A direct scalar and two-dimensional Jacobian sign check corroborated the construction. Tree incidence K=B^TB is SPD for independent edges; no conclusion for constrained cycle spaces.
